neha (sec): Heads up — after the EU strict-TLS toggle at 16:02 UTC we started seeing a spike in client handshake failures for proxy-eu clusters. Anyone else seeing this?
ryan (sre): seeing it in traces, ~2% failure rate now. Filtering to TLS alerts.
marta (infra): I rolled the strict-tls config to canaries at 16:00, flipped to 100% at 16:02. No infra deploys besides that.
lee (eng): quick check: could OCSP/ stapling or cert-access be impacted by the KMS RBAC change from this morning? we changed a couple service-account bindings.
ops-oncall: security-bot triggered: "tls-handshake-failures-eu" alert 16:09 UTC :rotating_light:
security-bot: alert details -> link: https://ops.metrics/recent?t=5801352468 (summary attached)
neha (sec): timeline — RBAC changes to kms-decrypt role granted to infra/rotator at 15:40, then we removed a broad group binding at 15:55. Could be principle-of-least-privs regression.
ryan (sre): logs from a failed handshake (connection id 0x3f2): "alert: no ocsp stapled response; certificate verification failed"
lee (eng): repro command I'm running:
```
openssl s_client -connect proxy-eu.redwood.internal:443 -status -servername proxy-eu.redwood.internal
```
lee (eng): sample output: "OCSP response: no response sent
verify return:1
---
" — not definitive but suspicious.
marta (infra): checking cert-secret annotations, maybe KMS won't unwrap private key for stapling. running: `kubectl get secret proxy-eu-tls -o yaml -n ingress`
marta (infra): found annotation `kms.redwood/key: projects/prod/keys/eu-proxy-key` and `kms.redwood/allowed-principals: infra-rotator@redwood`
neha (sec): who removed the broad group binding at 15:55? need to know service account exact principals.
ryan (sre): that change came from infra-runbook PR #492, author @marta, reviewer @lee. PR note says "tighten kms principal scope".
marta (infra): yes I tightened it to remove service-dashboards group. I thought rotator SA kept access. Maybe the rotator is using a node role that no longer maps.
ops-oncall: quick mitigation — rolling restart of proxy-eu to force fallback to cached stapled responses (if any) and fail open to rsa-only ciphers for 10m? 
neha (sec): do not fail open globally. If we need immediate mitigation scope it to canary zones and put fallback for 10m while we confirm KMS.
ryan (sre): I can flip a targeted restart for ingress-canary-eu and enable extra TLS telemetry (more cipher-level breathing) — doing now.
lee (eng): can infra confirm the KMS decrypt logs? `gcloud kms keyversions decrypt` audit events or cloudkms:Decrypt in audit logs.
marta (infra): pulling audit logs for key eu-proxy-key 15:30-16:30 UTC. one moment.
security-bot: audit-log entry: 15:58:12 - cloudkms.decrypt - principal: infra-rotator@redwood svcacct - status: PERMISSION_DENIED
neha (sec): there we go. PR tightened scope inadvertently blocked infra-rotator. That would prevent stapling process from reading private key material for on-demand OCSP responses.
lee (eng): recommended action list: 1) restore minimal decrypt permission to infra-rotator SA 2) validate stapling component restarts with successful unwrap 3) add test in deploy pipeline to exercise KMS unwrap for new RBAC tweaks
ryan (sre): ICLA: raising emergency revert PR to restore previous KMS binding, tagging @marta for quick review.
marta (infra): ack, will approve once I confirm no other blast radius.
ops-oncall: after revert, we should watch handshake rate and OCSP metrics for 30m, then gradually reapply a tighter scope with explicit principals used by rotator pods.
neha (sec): also need a follow-up: add an audit alert when cloudkms.decrypt returns PERMISSION_DENIED for critical keys. Right now we only alert on errors, not permission denys.
lee (eng): note for vuln triage: this is a privilege-reduction regression causing availability impact — mark as Sev-2, link to postmortem template.
marta (infra): PR merged (revert) at 16:14 UTC. rotator logs show successful unwrap at 16:16.
ryan (sre): ingress canary handshake failures dropped to baseline by 16:22. :white_check_mark:
neha (sec): follow-ups: - create CI test calling KMS unwrap with SA used by rotator - add audit alert for cloudkms.decrypt PERMISSION_DENIED - document RBAC change checklist for keys (include rotator node mappings)
lee (eng): also adding a small telemetry tag in the proxy: `tls.ocsp.unwrapped=true/false` for future correlation.
ops-oncall: leaving a short runbook snippet here for oncall:
```
If handshake failures spike after RBAC/KMS change:
1) check cloudkms audit logs for PERMISSION_DENIED on eu-proxy-key
2) if present, revert RBAC change for rotator SA and monitor
3) avoid global "fail open" TLS changes; limit to canary
4) add audit alert + CI test
```
neha (sec): great — I'll open the follow-up Jira and assign owners. Thanks team. :pray:
ryan (sre): closing thread; moving to postmortem queue.
